What Are the Main Complaints About Base44?

The main complaints in Base44 reviews are credit drain during debugging and slow customer support. Users on Trustpilot frequently report the AI burning through credits trying to fix errors it introduced, with support response times stretching days.

How Does Base44 Compare to Emergent?

The main difference between Base44 and Emergent is architecture and production depth. Emergent runs a multi-agent architecture where dedicated agents handle different layers of the build, keeping apps stable as they grow. Base44 uses a single-agent system that works well for simple builds but struggles once your app needs to handle conditional logic at scale.

Is Base44 Owned by Wix? [...] Who should avoid it:

   Teams building production-ready apps.It struggles with conditional logic and has had documented uptime issues.
   Developers who need full code control.GitHub integration requires the Builder plan, starting at $40/month (billed annually), and the exported code is AI-generated, which may need cleanup before handing off to a developer.
   Anyone on a tight budget.The credit system is unpredictable enough to make monthly costs hard to forecast.
   Projects requiring advanced design customization.If pixel-perfect UI matters, Base44's visual control will frustrate you.

## The Strongest Base44 Alternative: Emergent

If you want an app that holds up past the prototype stage, Emergent is worth a real look. [...] ❌ "To be honest, Lovable feels better right now, and I’m really frustrated because I already purchased a yearly Base44 plan, so I’m stuck here and need this to work." — Verified User, Reddit

## My Personal Review on Base44

I built a task management MVP on Base44, a simple internal tool for tracking projects and logging progress across a small team. I went inwith zero coding experienceand no developer to fall back on.

Within 20 minutes, the app was live and data was persisting between sessions. The Visual Editor let me adjust the layout without burning credits, which made that part of the build feel a lot less stressful.

Visual editor on top of code. After the AI generates the app, you can tweak colors, copy, and layout in a visual editor without re-prompting. This solves the common Lovable/Bolt pain point where every cosmetic change burns credits.

Lower total bill for small projects. No separate Supabase invoice, no Vercel Pro, no Auth0. For a single app at low traffic, $16/month on Base44 is genuinely cheaper than the comparable stack on Lovable.

Native integrations that work. Stripe checkout, Slack notifications, Google Sheets exports, SendGrid emails — all configured by the platform rather than requiring you to wire up API keys. This is where Base44 saves the most time for non-developers.

## What Base44 Breaks On

The cons are real and they matter: [...] What does Base44 do badly?
:   Three real limitations: (1) limited visual control over advanced design — sophisticated visual designs are hard to pull off, (2) unpredictable credit burn — the AI sometimes gets stuck and wastes credits on retries, (3) custom business logic complexity — it struggles with anything that needs intricate conditional flows or multi-step state machines. Also: the integrated database creates vendor lock-in. Migrating data out if you outgrow the platform is genuinely difficult. [...] Design control is limited. The visual editor is good for tweaks but not for fully custom design systems. If your brand requires a specific look (custom typography, intricate animations, unusual layouts), you'll hit walls. The styling system is constrained by what the AI templates support.

Vendor lock-in is real. This is the biggest one. The integrated database means your data lives in Base44's managed Postgres. Migrating off the platform is genuinely hard — there's no clean "export everything" button, and GitHub code export was still in beta on most plans as of mid-2026. If you build something successful, you're stuck on Base44 or facing a painful rebuild.
